title: Metering Service Billing Adjustments for Meters Found Inaccurate
content:
## Clauses in force

1. Under the **Metering Service**, a meter found fast is corrected by a refund, and a meter found slow or not registering is corrected by a backbill.
2. An adjustment smaller than the meter type's adjustment threshold is recorded with an amount of 0.00 and posts nothing.
3. Each test result is adjusted once. A test result that already carries an accuracy adjustment on the meter's adjustment record is not adjusted again.
4. Backbills never attract a late payment charge, and a backbill for a residential customer may be placed in a payment arrangement under the Payment Arrangement program's terms.

| Test result | Direction of the adjustment |
|---|---|
| Fast | Refund |
| Slow | Backbill |
| Not registering | Backbill |
| Within tolerance | No adjustment |

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of this rule are **no longer in force**. They are kept here as the record of the earlier rule and are superseded by the current basis for each kind of adjustment.

- (a) No longer in force: the adjustment period ends on the test date and starts on the error start date, which applies the meter type's error-start basis and caps the period at the refund limit for a refund or the backbill limit for a backbill. The error start date was the later of the midpoint between the later of the installed date and the latest earlier test date on the installation, and the test date, rounded down to a whole day, and the test date less the refund limit or the backbill limit in calendar months.
- (b) No longer in force: the corrected charges are the energy, demand and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of the regular bills whose billing period ends inside the adjustment period, that is after the adjustment start date and on or before the test date.
- (c) No longer in force: for a fast or slow meter, the amount is those charges times the absolute value of one minus 100 divided by the registration percentage, and the adjusted kWh is their kWh total times the same factor, both rounded at the end.
- (d) No longer in force: for a meter found not registering, the backbill is computed under the meter type's non-registering usage basis.
- (e) No longer in force: the refund is credited, and the backbill billed, on the service agreement on the adjustment date.

## Points of judgement on the clauses in force

- **Threshold (hypothetical amount).** For a type whose threshold is 5.00, a calculated adjustment of 4.80 is recorded as 0.00 and posts nothing; 5.00 is posted.
- **Once per result.** A second adjustment against a test result already adjusted is not made, whatever its direction.
- **Residential backbill.** The backbill itself never carries a late payment charge; whether it is placed in a payment arrangement is decided under that program's own terms.

title: Metering Service Schedule of Accuracy Test Terms
content:
Accuracy tolerance, test method and test charges for every meter type of the **Metering Service** are fixed per type as follows. A meter registers accurately when its registration lies within 100 percent plus or minus the type's tolerance, in percentage points.

## Tolerance, method and timing

| Meter type | Accuracy tolerance (percentage points) | Accurate band of registration | Test method of the type (where a customer-requested test is performed) | Business days after the request within which the test is performed | Customer may witness the test | Meter found non-registering or outside tolerance is replaced within |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 to 102.00 | Meter shop (meter exchanged and shop-tested) | 10 | Yes | 5 business days |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 to 102.00 | Meter shop | 10 | Yes | 5 business days |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 to 102.00 | Meter shop | 10 | Yes | 5 business days |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 to 102.00 | Field (tested in place) | 15 | Yes | 10 business days |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 1.0 | 99.00 to 101.00 | Field | 15 | Yes | 10 business days |
| Primary Metering Installation | 0.5 | 99.50 to 100.50 | Field | 20 | Yes | 10 business days |

## Free tests, repeat test fee and periodic testing

| Meter type | Free customer-requested tests per period | Free-test period (months) | Repeat test fee (USD) | Repeat test fee waived when the meter is found outside tolerance | Periodic test interval (years) | Fee for a periodic or utility-initiated test (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 1 | 12 | 45.00 | Yes | 0 (statistical sample testing only) | 0.00 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 1 | 12 | 45.00 | Yes | 0 (statistical sample testing only) | 0.00 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 1 | 12 | 45.00 | Yes | 0 (statistical sample testing only) | 0.00 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 1 | 12 | 85.00 | Yes | 8 | 0.00 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 1 | 12 | 150.00 | Yes | 4 | 0.00 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 1 | 12 | 375.00 | Yes | 2 | 0.00 |

A periodic test interval of 0 years means the type is not tested on an installation-by-installation schedule; it is covered by statistical sample testing only.

## Notes on the schedule

- **Band edges are inside the band.** For a type with a 2.0-point tolerance, a registration of exactly 98.00 or exactly 102.00 is accurate; 97.99 and 102.01 are not. For the Primary Metering Installation, 99.50 and 100.50 are accurate; 99.49 and 100.51 are not.
- **Periodic and utility-initiated tests are never charged.** Their fee is 0.00 for every type.
- **Hypothetical illustration.** A customer-requested test of an AMI Interval Demand Meter is performed in the field, may be witnessed, and, where it is chargeable as a repeat test, carries the 150.00 repeat test fee of that type.

title: Metering Service Training Note: The Free Test Allowance Belongs to the Agreement
content:
The free-test allowance of the **Metering Service** belongs to the service agreement, not to a single meter.

## The rule

Customer-requested tests on every installation of the same service agreement count together, so exchanging a meter after a test does not renew the allowance. Tests at different service agreements of the same customer are counted separately. Periodic, utility-initiated and Commission referee tests never count toward the allowance.

**What is counted.** For a test under review, the count is the number of test requests with the reason "customer request" recorded on any meter installation of the same service agreement whose request date falls in the window: the meter type's free-test period, in calendar months, ending the day before the request date of the test under review. The test under review is therefore not part of its own count.

## Questions this rule answers

**Does a new meter come with a new free test?** No. Customer-requested tests on the removed meter and on the new meter of the same agreement are counted together.

**Does a test at the customer's other address use up this agreement's allowance?** No. Each service agreement is counted on its own.

**Do company-scheduled tests use the allowance?** No. Periodic, utility-initiated and Commission referee tests are never counted.

## Worked count (hypothetical dates, 12-month free-test period)

A customer-requested test is requested on 15 March 2025. The window runs from 15 March 2024 to 14 March 2025.

| Earlier request on the same agreement | Counted? |
|---|---|
| Customer request on 20 May 2024, on the meter since exchanged | Yes |
| Periodic test request on 1 August 2024 | No (periodic) |
| Customer request on 10 March 2024 | No (before the window) |
| Customer request on 2 January 2025 at the customer's other agreement | No (different agreement) |

The count for the 15 March 2025 test is 1.

title: Metering Service Billing Adjustment Limits and Bases by Meter Type
content:
The figures below are the **Metering Service** limits and bases that bound a billing adjustment for a meter test result, fixed per meter type.

## Period limits and posting threshold

| Meter type | Longest refund period, ending on the test date (months) | Longest backbill period, ending on the test date (months) | Smallest adjustment that is posted (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 12 | 6 | 1.00 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 12 | 6 | 1.00 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 12 | 6 | 1.00 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 12 | 12 | 5.00 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 12 | 12 | 5.00 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 24 | 12 | 25.00 |

In this knowledge base, "the meter type's refund limit" means the longest refund period above, "the meter type's backbill limit" means the longest backbill period above, and "the meter type's adjustment threshold" means the smallest adjustment that is posted.

## Bases recorded for each type

| Basis | Value |
|---|---|
| Error-start basis, used where no record shows when the error began (all types) | Midpoint between the later of the installed date and the last previous test date, and the test date |
| Charges corrected by an accuracy adjustment (all types) | Energy, demand and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of each regular bill in the adjustment period |
| Rounding of adjustment kWh and amounts (all types) | Amount rounded to the cent after summing all affected bills |
| Rates that price corrected usage (all types) | Rates of the schedule in effect for each affected bill |
| Usage basis for a meter found not registering: Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter, Standard AMI Smart Meter, AMI Bidirectional Net Meter, AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | kWh of the same billing periods of the prior year, priced at the rates of the affected bills |
| Usage basis for a meter found not registering: AMI Interval Demand Meter, Primary Metering Installation | kWh and demand of the same billing periods of the prior year, priced at the rates of the affected bills |

## Reading the table

- The refund limit is 12 months for every type except the Primary Metering Installation, at 24.
- The backbill limit is 6 months for the three residential-class types and 12 months for the three commercial types.
- **Threshold boundary (hypothetical amounts).** For an AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter, a calculated adjustment of 4.99 is below the 5.00 threshold; 5.00 is not below it.

title: Commission Referee Testing of Metering Service Meters: Fees and Request Window
content:
After a company accuracy test, a **Metering Service** customer who disputes the result may ask for a Commission referee test wherever the meter type allows it. The fee the customer pays for a referee test is refunded if the referee finds the meter outside tolerance.

| Meter type | Referee test available | Referee test fee (USD) | Calendar days after the company test date within which a referee test may be requested |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Yes | 25.00 | 30 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | Yes | 25.00 | 30 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | Yes | 25.00 | 30 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | Yes | 50.00 | 30 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | Yes | 50.00 | 30 |
| Primary Metering Installation | Yes | 100.00 | 30 |

## Points of reference

- Every meter type allows a referee test, and every type has the same 30-day request window.
- The fee differs by type: 25.00 for the three residential-class types, 50.00 for the AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter and the AMI Interval Demand Meter, and 100.00 for the Primary Metering Installation.
- **Fee outcome (hypothetical results).** A customer with an AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter pays the 50.00 referee fee. If the referee finds the meter outside tolerance, the 50.00 is refunded; if the referee finds it within tolerance, the fee stays paid.

title: Demand Charges Corrected by a Metering Service Fast-Meter Refund
content:
On an Electric Service Agreement whose rate schedule carries a demand charge, the demand charges a **Metering Service** fast-meter refund corrects depend on the billing demand of the covered bills.

## Clause

Where the service agreement's rate schedule carries a demand charge and at least one bill the fast-meter refund covers was billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand, the charges the fast-meter refund corrects are the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of every covered bill plus the demand charges of the covered bills billed above that minimum.

Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and no covered bill was billed at the minimum billing demand, the charges the fast-meter refund corrects are the energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of every covered bill.

Where the rate schedule carries no demand charge, no demand charge is corrected.

## Points of judgement

- A covered bill was billed at the minimum billing demand when the billing demand on that bill, in kW, equals the schedule's minimum billing demand.
- One bill at the minimum is enough to exclude the demand charges of every bill held at the minimum; the bills above it are still corrected.

## Hypothetical example

A schedule with a demand charge and a 30 kW minimum billing demand; three covered bills with billing demands of 30, 41 and 45 kW and demand charges of 240.00, 328.00 and 360.00. The first bill sits at the minimum, so the demand charges corrected are 328.00 plus 360.00, that is 688.00. With billing demands of 31, 41 and 45 kW, all three demand charges, 928.00 in the hypothetical, would be corrected.

title: Metering Service Rule on Dating a Fast Meter's Error: Drift and Schedule Changes
content:
The billing months a **Metering Service** fast-meter refund reaches back follow what the meter's records show about when the over-registration began, and they never reach back past the meter's latest within-tolerance result, which is the company's evidence that the meter registered within tolerance on that date.

**Drift toward the limit.** Where the meter's latest within-tolerance result already lay in the outer drift share of 0.75 of the tolerance band, on the same side of 100 as the company test's registration percentage, the meter was drifting toward the limit at that test, so the error is dated from that test itself rather than from the midpoint, and the billing months the fast-meter refund reaches back are all the whole calendar months between the test date of that within-tolerance result and the company test date.

**Schedule change.** Where the latest within-tolerance result shows no such drift and the Electric Service Agreement's current rate schedule took effect after its test date, the billing months the fast-meter refund reaches back are the whole calendar months between the schedule's effective date and the company test date.

**Every other case.** Neither dating applies.

## Drift thresholds by meter type

A within-tolerance result is in the outer drift share when it lies at least 0.75 of the type's tolerance away from 100. Because the company test found the meter fast, above 100, the drift must also lie above 100.

| Meter type | Tolerance | Latest within-tolerance result counts as drift when it is at or above |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 2.0 | 101.50 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 2.0 | 101.50 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 2.0 | 101.50 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 2.0 | 101.50 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 1.0 | 100.75 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 0.5 | 100.375 |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, tolerance 2.0, company test fast at 103.00)

| Latest within-tolerance result | Drift? | Reach-back |
|---|---|---|
| 101.50 on 10 April 2024 | Yes | All whole calendar months from 10 April 2024 to the company test date |
| 101.49 on 10 April 2024 | No | Schedule dating if the current schedule took effect after 10 April 2024; otherwise neither dating |
| 98.30 on 10 April 2024 | No, it lies below 100, the opposite side | As for the row above |

title: Late Payment Charges Returned With a Metering Service Fast-Meter Refund
content:
Late payment charges posted on the Electric Service Agreement within the whole calendar months the **Metering Service** fast-meter refund covers, counted from the handling date as the covered bills are, were computed on overstated bills. These are the late payment charges posted in the same months, reckoned back from the handling date, as the bills the refund covers.

**General service schedules.** Where the agreement is on a general service schedule (GS, GST, GD or LP) and such late payment charges exist, the corrected late payment charges are those charges times the fast-meter error factor, rounded to the cent.

**Residential schedules.** Where the agreement is on a residential schedule (RS, RT or REV) and such late payment charges exist, the corrected late payment charges are all of those charges.

**No such charges.** Where no late payment charge was posted within those months, no late payment charge is corrected.

## Decision table

| Schedule of the agreement | Late payment charges posted within the covered months | Corrected late payment charges |
|---|---|---|
| GS, GST, GD or LP | Yes | Those charges times the fast-meter error factor, rounded to the cent |
| RS, RT or REV | Yes | All of those charges |
| Any | None | None |

## Hypothetical cases

- Schedule GS, late payment charges of 12.00 and 9.60 within the covered months, fast-meter error factor of 0.0291262: 21.60 times 0.0291262 is 0.63 after rounding to the cent.
- Schedule RT with the same two late payment charges: all 21.60 is returned.

title: Bills Ending After the Company Test in a Metering Service Fast-Meter Refund
content:
Whether a **Metering Service** fast-meter refund also covers regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement ending after the company test date depends on whether, and when, the meter was taken out of service.

1. Where the meter was removed from service after the company test date, the fast-meter refund also covers the regular bills whose billing period ended after the company test date and on or before the removal date, added to the bills counted back from the company test date, because the meter kept registering fast until it was taken out.
2. Where the meter is still in service, the fast-meter refund also covers every regular bill whose billing period ended after the company test date, added to the bills counted back.
3. In every other case, a meter removed on or before the company test date among them, no bill whose billing period ended after the company test date is added.

The installation's status and removal date are read from the meter installation record.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical, company test on 12 May, bills ending on the last day of each month)

- **Removed 3 July.** Removed after the company test date: the bills ending 31 May and 30 June are added; the bill ending 31 July ended after the removal date and is not.
- **Removed 12 May.** Not removed after the company test date: nothing is added.
- **In service, handling date 20 August.** Every regular bill ending after 12 May is added: those ending 31 May, 30 June and 31 July.

title: Computation of the Fast-Meter Refund, Metering Service
content:
The **Metering Service** fast-meter refund is the amount defined in the clause below, computed from the company test result, the regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement at the premise, and the meter's metering charges.

## Clause

(1) The company test is the latest test result of the meter taken by the test method of the meter's type; its date is the company test date and its registration percentage is the company test's registration.

(2) The fast-meter refund covers whole regular bills of the service agreement: counting back from the company test date, the most recent regular bills whose billing period ended on or before that date, as many as the smaller of the billing months the fast-meter refund reaches back and the fast-meter refund limit, and no bill whose billing period ended after the company test date.

(3) The billing months the fast-meter refund reaches back are one half of the whole calendar months between the later of the meter's installation date and the test date of its latest within-tolerance result, and the company test date, rounded down to a whole month. The fast-meter refund limit is the meter type's refund limit.

(4) The charges the fast-meter refund corrects are the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of those bills, and the fast-meter error factor is the absolute value of one minus 100 divided by the company test's registration. No late payment charge is corrected and no interest is added, so the corrected late payment charges and the refund interest are each 0.00.

(5) The fast-meter refund is the corrected charges times the fast-meter error factor, rounded to the cent, plus the corrected late payment charges, plus the refund interest, plus every repeat test fee standing on the meter's metering charges, which the refund returns because the meter was in fact inaccurate. A fast-meter refund smaller than the meter type's adjustment threshold is recorded as 0.00.

Whole calendar months are counted from a day of one month to the same day of a later month.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Installation date | 1 March 2022 |
| Latest within-tolerance result | 1 March 2023 |
| Company test | 20 March 2025, registration 103.00 |
| Meter type's refund limit and adjustment threshold | 12 months and 1.00 |
| Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of the 12 most recent regular bills ending on or before 20 March 2025 | 1,800.00 and 300.00 |
| Repeat test fees standing on the meter's metering charges | One fee of 45.00 |

- Later of installation and latest within-tolerance date: 1 March 2023. Whole calendar months to 20 March 2025: 24. One half: 12. The smaller of 12 and the 12-month limit: 12 bills.
- Corrected charges: 2,100.00. Error factor: the absolute value of one minus 100 divided by 103, that is 0.0291262.
- 2,100.00 times 0.0291262 is 61.17 after rounding to the cent.
- Refund: 61.17 plus 0.00 plus 0.00 plus 45.00, that is 106.17, which is not below 1.00.

title: Fast-Meter Refunds Under the Metering Service: Desk Guidance and Posting
content:
A fast-meter refund returns what a **Metering Service** meter over-registered, and it is calculated for the company's own test result of the meter, which is the latest test result taken by the test method of the meter's type, when that result classifies the meter fast; it is recorded on the meter's adjustment record against that result, as a refund, on the date it is calculated.

**When the amount is fixed.** The fast-meter refund is fixed only after every repeat test fee owed for the meter's earlier within-tolerance customer tests stands on the meter's metering charges. Stated from the records' side: so long as a repeat test fee owed for one of the meter's earlier within-tolerance customer tests is not standing on the meter's metering charges, the refund amount is not yet fixed.

## Records that show the refund's position

| Record | What it shows |
|---|---|
| The meter's test results | The company test, the latest result by the meter type's test method (meter shop or field), classifies the meter fast; earlier within-tolerance results of customer-requested tests |
| The meter's metering charges | The repeat test fees standing on the meter |
| The meter's adjustment record | The fast-meter refund, once recorded, against the company test result |

## Recording the refund: `post_fast_meter_refund_06e0a347`

**Capability.** The tool records the fast-meter refund that Lakeshore calculates for the company's own accuracy test of a meter that registered too much energy. One call adds one refund entry to the meter's adjustment record, dated today and tied to the test result it corrects; the entry carries the refund amount in US dollars that is owed back to the customer for the meter's error. Nothing else on the meter or the service account is changed by the call.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool, unlocked with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then called with `call_agent_discoverable_tool` under its name, `post_fast_meter_refund_06e0a347`.

**Parameters.**

1. `meter_installation_id` — the meter installation reference number of the meter whose registration was found fast, as returned by the meter installation lookup; identifier text.
2. `meter_test_id` — the reference number of the test result, not the test request, that the refund corrects, as returned by the meter test lookup for that meter; identifier text.
3. `refund_amount` — the refund in US dollars, a non-negative number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed; 0.00 records a refund below the posting threshold.

**Return.** One confirmation line: "Fast-meter refund (adjustment reference) recorded on meter (installation reference) for test result (test result reference): (amount) USD on (date)." The adjustment reference is the new entry's reference number, the amount carries 2 decimals and the date is today's adjustment date. Receiving the line means the refund entry exists on the meter's adjustment record and shows when the meter's adjustments are looked up.

title: Interest on Metering Service Fast-Meter Refunds
content:
Interest on a **Metering Service** fast-meter refund turns on the number of bills the refund counts back from the company test date.

| Bills counted back from the company test date | Refund interest rate |
|---|---|
| 12 or more (the full-interest number) | 4.17 percent (0.0417) |
| At least 3 (the half-interest number) and fewer than 12 | One half of 4.17 percent, that is 2.085 percent |
| Fewer than 3 | No refund interest |

**Clause.** Where the fast-meter refund counts back at least the full-interest number of 12 bills, the refund interest rate is the refund interest rate of 4.17 percent. Where it covers at least the half-interest number of 3 bills but fewer than 12, the refund interest rate is one half of the refund interest rate. In every other case there is no refund interest.

**Amount.** The refund interest is the corrected charges times the fast-meter error factor, rounded to the cent, times the refund interest rate, times the number of bills counted back from the company test date divided by 24, which is simple interest for half the counted-back period in years, rounded to the cent. Only the bills counted back from the company test date are counted; a bill whose billing period ended after the company test date is not.

## Worked figures (hypothetical, corrected charges times the error factor, rounded, of 61.17)

| Bills counted back | Rate | Interest |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | 4.17 percent | 61.17 times 0.0417 times 12 divided by 24 is 1.28 |
| 6 | 2.085 percent | 61.17 times 0.02085 times 6 divided by 24 is 0.32 |
| 3 | 2.085 percent | 61.17 times 0.02085 times 3 divided by 24 is 0.16 |
| 2 | None | 0.00 |
| 11 | 2.085 percent | 61.17 times 0.02085 times 11 divided by 24 is 0.58 |

title: Fast-Meter Refund Limits on Large Power and Medium Demand Schedules, Metering Service
content:
The rate schedule of the Electric Service Agreement decides the limit on the number of bills a **Metering Service** fast-meter refund counts back.

| Electric Service Agreement schedule | Fast-meter refund limit |
|---|---|
| Schedule LP Large Power Service | 3 months, the large-power refund limit |
| Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service | 6 months, the medium-demand refund limit |
| Any other schedule | No large-power or medium-demand limit applies |

**Clause.** Where the agreement is on Schedule LP, the fast-meter refund limit is the large-power refund limit of 3 months. Where the agreement is on Schedule GD, the fast-meter refund limit is the medium-demand refund limit of 6 months.

**Reading the schedule.** The schedule is the one the service agreement is on, as its record shows, not the schedule the meter type could bill.

**Hypothetical cases.** A Primary Metering Installation on an agreement served under Schedule LP Large Power Service has a 3-month limit; an AMI Interval Demand Meter on Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service has a 6-month limit; a Standard AMI Smart Meter on Schedule RS Residential Standard Service has neither.

title: Rule on Meter Installations Held at a Service Agreement (Metering Service)
content:
**Rule.** Under the **Metering Service**, each service agreement has one meter in service at a time. A customer may hold meter installations at every service agreement the customer has, and there is no limit on the number of installations one customer may hold across those agreements. The same agreement accumulates installations over time as meters are exchanged.

**One open order per agreement.** No other installation order for the same service agreement is in scheduled status. The company's installation records decide this, read for the service agreement named on the new order: where an order for that agreement already stands in scheduled status, a further order for the same agreement is not placed alongside it. An order for a different service agreement of the same customer is unaffected.

**Exchange.** An exchange is made by ordering the new meter while the old one is in service; the old meter is removed on the day the new one is installed.

## The rule in condition and result form

| Condition, read from the installation records | Result |
|---|---|
| The agreement has no installation order in scheduled status | A new installation order may be placed for that agreement |
| The agreement already has an installation order in scheduled status | No second order for the same agreement is placed |
| The agreement's current meter is in service and a new meter is ordered | The new meter is the exchange; the old meter is removed on the new meter's installation day |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A customer holds two agreements, one for a home and one for a shop. A scheduled order at the home agreement does not prevent an order at the shop agreement.
- An agreement's meter was exchanged twice over the years. The agreement now shows three installations: two removed and one in service; only the one in service is the meter in service.

title: Ordering, Installing and Removing Meters Under the Metering Service
content:
**Ordering.** A **Metering Service** meter type may be ordered only for a service agreement whose rate schedule is among the type's supported schedules and whose capabilities the agreement needs: a time-of-use schedule needs a time-of-use capable meter, a demand schedule needs a demand register, a net energy metering agreement needs a bidirectional meter, and service at primary voltage needs the Primary Metering Installation.

**Installation date.** The installation date is no earlier than the meter type's installation lead time, in business days, after the order date.

**In service and removal.** The installed meter becomes in service on its installation date, and the meter it replaces is removed the same day.

**Withdrawal and reuse.** An order may be withdrawn while it is scheduled. A removed or cancelled installation is never reused; a later need is met by a new order.

## Installation statuses

| Status | Meaning | Moves to |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduled | Ordered, not yet installed | In service, when the field crew installs the meter and it starts registering for billing; or cancelled, when the order is withdrawn before installation at the customer's request or because the service start was cancelled |
| In service | Registering for billing | Removed, when the meter is taken out of service for exchange, shop testing, an opt-out or return, or because the service agreement closed |
| Removed | Out of service | Never reused |
| Cancelled | Order withdrawn | Never reused |

## Capability needs (worked from the rule)

| The agreement has | The meter ordered must be |
|---|---|
| A time-of-use schedule | Time-of-use capable |
| A demand schedule | Fitted with a demand register |
| A net energy metering agreement | Bidirectional |
| Service at primary voltage | The Primary Metering Installation |

**Hypothetical case.** An agreement on Schedule RT Residential Time-of-Use Service is a time-of-use agreement, so the meter type ordered for it must both list Schedule RT among its supported schedules and be time-of-use capable.

title: Metering Service Meter Reading Schedule: Read Method, Estimates and Customer Reads
content:
How each **Metering Service** meter type is read, how long estimates may run, and whether a customer's own reading is accepted are fixed per type as follows.

## Read method and estimate limits

| Meter type | Read method | Months between field reads | Consecutive estimated bills after which the next read must be an actual field read | Business days within which that field read is made | Consecutive failed field-read visits after which an access letter is sent and a self-read is requested |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Manual | 2 | 2 | 10 | 2 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | Remote | 0 (remotely read) | 2 | 10 | 2 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | Remote | 0 (remotely read) | 1 | 5 | 2 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | Remote | 0 (remotely read) | 2 | 10 | 2 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | Remote | 0 (remotely read) | 1 | 5 | 2 |
| Primary Metering Installation | Remote | 0 (remotely read) | 1 | 3 | 1 |

## Customer readings

| Meter type | Customer-submitted reading used for billing in months without a company read | Calendar days before the billing period end within which a customer reading is accepted |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Yes | 3 |
| All five other types | No | 0 (not accepted) |

## Estimate method and true-up

| Meter type | How an estimated reading is computed | How estimated usage is reconciled at the next read |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | kWh of the same billing period of the prior year scaled by the ratio of billing days | The next actual or customer read replaces the estimated register reading and the difference is billed or credited on the next bill |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter, AMI Bidirectional Net Meter, AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | kWh of the same billing period of the prior year scaled by the ratio of billing days | The next actual read replaces the estimated register reading and the difference is billed or credited on the next bill |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter, Primary Metering Installation | kWh and demand of the same billing period of the prior year scaled by the ratio of billing days | The next actual read replaces the estimated register reading and the difference is billed or credited on the next bill |

## Points of reference

- Only the Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter is read manually, and only it accepts a customer reading.
- **Hypothetical estimate.** A Standard AMI Smart Meter billing period of 31 days whose same period a year earlier ran 30 days and registered 600 kWh is estimated at 600 kWh scaled by 31 over 30, that is 620 kWh.

title: Meter Reading, Estimated Bills and Field Access Under the Metering Service
content:
**Reading.** Remotely read **Metering Service** meters are read on every billing period end date. Manually read meters are field-read at the meter type's field-read interval in months and estimated under the type's estimate method in between, unless a customer reading is accepted. A customer reading is used only where the meter type accepts customer readings and the reading is submitted within the type's customer-read window, in calendar days, before the billing period end.

**Estimate limit.** The number of consecutive estimates is the count of the installation's most recent readings, up to the handling date and taken most recent first, that are estimated. When that count reaches the meter type's estimate limit, the next reading must be an actual field read made within the type's field-read period in business days.

**Access failures.** A failed field visit is recorded as an access failure. After the meter type's access-failure threshold of consecutive failures, an access letter is sent and a customer reading is requested.

**One reading per period.** Each billing period end date has one reading per installation; a period end date that already carries a reading for the installation receives no second reading.

**True-up.** Estimated usage is reconciled under the meter type's true-up rule, which posts the difference on the service agreement as a backbill for an estimated-read true-up or as a billing error correction credit.

## Condition and result

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Remote read method | Read on every billing period end date |
| Manual read method, month between field reads | Estimated, unless an accepted customer reading exists |
| Customer reading submitted inside the window, type accepts customer reads | Used for billing |
| Consecutive estimates reach the estimate limit | Next reading is an actual field read within the type's period |
| Consecutive failed visits reach the access-failure threshold | Access letter sent and a customer reading requested |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- An estimate limit of 2: the installation's last two readings are estimated and the one before is actual. The count of consecutive estimates is 2, so the next reading must be an actual field read.
- A customer-read window of 3 days and a billing period ending on the 30th: a customer reading submitted on the 27th, 28th, 29th or 30th is inside the window; one submitted on the 26th is not.

title: Metering Service Tariff Rule: Accuracy Test Requests and Commission Referee Tests
content:
**1. Who may ask, and for which meter.** The customer of record may ask for an accuracy test of the meter in service at any of the customer's service agreements at any time under the **Metering Service**; the request is recorded with the test reason "customer request". A test is requested only for a meter installation in in-service status, as the company's installation record for that installation shows; an installation that is scheduled, removed or cancelled is not tested.

**2. Scheduling.** The scheduled date is no later than the meter type's test completion period, in business days, after the request date, counting business days as Monday through Friday excluding company holidays.

**3. Witnessing.** Where the meter type allows a witnessed test, the customer may ask to witness it.

**4. Commission referee test.** After a company test, a customer who disputes the result may ask for a Commission referee test where the meter type allows a referee test. The referee test must be requested no later than the referee request window after the company test date. The window is counted in calendar days from the day after the company test date, and a request on the last day is accepted. The window is 30 calendar days for every meter type. The company test date is the test date the company's test record shows for the result being disputed. The referee test fee is paid by the customer and refunded if the referee finds the meter outside tolerance.

**5. Periodic tests.** Periodic tests are scheduled by the company every periodic test interval, for meter types that have an interval.

**6. Bills during a test.** A test request does not suspend bills, but the late payment charge on bills issued before the request is deferred under the service agreement's late payment rule while the test has no recorded result.

## The referee window at its boundary (hypothetical dates, 30-day window)

| Company test date | Day 1 of the window | Last day of the window | Referee request on | Within the window? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 June | 11 June | 10 July | 10 July | Yes, the last day is accepted |
| 10 June | 11 June | 10 July | 11 July | No, it is after the last day |
| 10 June | 11 June | 10 July | 25 June | Yes |

## Scheduling at its boundary (hypothetical)

A request made on a Monday for a type with a 10-business-day completion period, in a fortnight with no company holidays, is scheduled no later than the Monday two weeks later; a scheduled date on the Tuesday after that is outside the period.

## Points of judgement

- The test date that starts the referee window comes from the company's test record, not from the date the customer says the test happened.
- A request made while the meter installation is in service meets the status condition; the customer's description of the meter does not substitute for the installation record.

title: Metering Service Equipment Catalogue: Meter Types and Their Capabilities
content:
Lakeshore Power & Light sets one of six meter types at a premise under the **Metering Service**. Each type has a fixed ANSI C12 accuracy class and a fixed set of capabilities, and each is set only where its placement conditions hold.

## Placement conditions by meter type

| Meter type | Where the type is set |
|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Schedule RS Residential Standard Service or Schedule GS Small General Service, no net energy metering, and the customer's own opt-out election |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | Schedule RS, RT, REV, GS or GST service, single phase |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | Net energy metering required, single phase |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | Business customer, three-phase service, Schedule GS Small General Service or Schedule GST Small General Time-of-Use Service |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | Business customer on Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service |
| Primary Metering Installation | Business customer served at primary voltage on Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service or Schedule LP Large Power Service |

## Capabilities

| Meter type | Accuracy class | Remote disconnect and reconnect | Interval data | Time-of-use registers | Delivered and received registered separately | 15-minute demand register |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | No | None (0 minutes) | No | No | No |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | Yes | 60 minutes | Yes | No | No |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | Yes | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | No |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.5 | No | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | No |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | ANSI C12.20 class 0.2 | No | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Primary Metering Installation | ANSI C12.20 class 0.2 with instrument transformers | No | 15 minutes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

"Time-of-use registers" means the meter records on-peak, off-peak and super off-peak usage for time-of-use schedules. "Delivered and received registered separately" is the bidirectional registration that net energy metering requires.

## Schedules each type can bill, and installation lead time

| Meter type | Rate schedules the type can bill | Business days from order to earliest installation date |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | Schedules RS and GS | 5 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | Schedules RS, RT, REV, GS and GST | 5 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | Schedules RS, RT, REV, GS and GST with a net energy metering rider | 10 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | Schedules GS and GST | 10 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | Schedule GD | 15 |
| Primary Metering Installation | Schedules GD and LP served at primary voltage | 30 |

## Reading the catalogue

- **Remote switching.** Only the Standard AMI Smart Meter and the AMI Bidirectional Net Meter can disconnect and reconnect service remotely; every other type, the Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter included, cannot.
- **Demand.** Only the AMI Interval Demand Meter and the Primary Metering Installation carry a demand register.
- **Accuracy class.** The two demand-capable types are class 0.2; the other four are class 0.5.
- **Example (hypothetical order date).** A Primary Metering Installation ordered on a Monday with no company holidays in the following six weeks can be installed no earlier than the 30th business day after that Monday.

title: Computation of the Non-Registering Backbill, Metering Service
content:
The **Metering Service** non-registering backbill is the amount defined below from the meter's test results and the regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement at the premise.

1. **Non-registering test date.** The test date of the meter's latest result classifying it not registering.
2. **Covered bills.** The non-registering backbill covers whole regular bills of the service agreement: counting back from the non-registering test date, the most recent regular bills whose billing period ended on or before that date, as many as one half of the whole calendar months between the later of the meter's installation date and the test date of its latest within-tolerance result and the non-registering test date, rounded down, and never more than the meter type's backbill limit.
3. **Usage from the prior year.** The usage of each covered bill is taken from the regular bill of the same billing month one year earlier, so that the charges the non-registering backbill recovers are the energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of those prior-year bills, as billed, minus the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges already billed on the covered bills.
4. **Shares.** The overdue-test share and the reporting share are both 1.
5. **Backbill.** The non-registering backbill is the recovered charges multiplied first by the overdue-test share and then by the reporting share, rounded to the cent once at the end. A non-registering backbill smaller than the meter type's adjustment threshold is recorded as 0.00.

Whole calendar months are counted from a day of one month to the same day of a later month.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

- Installed 4 January 2021; latest within-tolerance result 4 January 2024; non-registering test 4 January 2025. Whole calendar months from 4 January 2024 to 4 January 2025: 12; one half: 6. With a backbill limit of 12 months, 6 bills are covered: the six most recent regular bills ending on or before 4 January 2025.
- The six regular bills of the same billing months one year earlier show energy charges of 720.00, Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of 120.00 and demand charges of 0.00, 840.00 in all.
- The six covered bills already billed energy charges of 90.00 and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of 15.00, 105.00 in all.
- Recovered charges: 840.00 less 105.00, that is 735.00. Multiplied by 1 and then by 1, rounded to the cent: 735.00, which is not below a hypothetical 5.00 threshold.

## Cap at the backbill limit

With a 6-month backbill limit, a meter whose half-span works out to 9 months is backbilled for 6 covered bills.

title: Non-Registering Meter Backbills Under the Metering Service: Desk Guidance and Posting
content:
A non-registering backbill recovers the usage a **Metering Service** meter failed to register, and it is calculated for the meter's test result that classifies it not registering; it is recorded on the meter's adjustment record against that result, as a backbill, on the date it is calculated.

**Records.** The meter's test results show the result classifying the meter not registering; the meter's adjustment record shows the non-registering backbill once recorded against that result.

## Recording the backbill: `post_non_registering_backbill_96d206ff`

**Capability.** The tool records the backbill that Lakeshore calculates for a meter whose accuracy test found it not registering energy at all. One call adds one backbill entry to the meter's adjustment record, dated today and tied to the test result that found the meter not registering; the entry carries the backbill amount in US dollars for the usage the meter failed to record. Nothing else on the meter or the service account is changed by the call.

**How it is invoked.** Agent-side: the representative unlocks `post_non_registering_backbill_96d206ff` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `meter_installation_id` | The meter installation reference number of the meter found not registering, as returned by the meter installation lookup | Identifier text |
| `meter_test_id` | The reference number of the test result, not the test request, that found the meter not registering, as returned by the meter test lookup for that meter | Identifier text |
| `backbill_amount` | The backbill in US dollars | A non-negative number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed; 0.00 records a backbill below the posting threshold |

**Return.** A one-line confirmation: "Non-registering backbill (adjustment reference) recorded on meter (installation reference) for test result (test result reference): (amount) USD on (date)." The adjustment reference is the new entry's reference number, the amount carries 2 decimals and the date is today's adjustment date. Receiving the line means the backbill entry exists on the meter's adjustment record and shows when the meter's adjustments are looked up.

**Illustration (hypothetical references).** A call for installation MI-0107 and test result MT-0311 with a backbill amount of 735.00 returns a line stating that a non-registering backbill of 735.00 USD was recorded on meter MI-0107 for test result MT-0311 on the current date.

title: Metering Service Rule on the Bills Covered When a Meter Stops Registering
content:
How many regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement a **Metering Service** non-registering backbill covers depends first on whether the stop is visible on the bills.

**Zero-kWh bills.** Where the service agreement's regular bills ending within the meter type's backbill limit before the non-registering test date include bills with zero kWh registered, the stop is visible on the bills and the non-registering backbill covers as many of the most recent bills as there are such zero-kWh bills.

**Set by replacement or exchange, never found accurate.** Where no such zero-kWh bill exists, the meter was set by a failed-meter replacement or a test exchange, and it has no within-tolerance test result on record, the non-registering backbill covers all the whole calendar months between the installation date and the non-registering test date, never more than the meter type's backbill limit.

**Every other case.** Neither of these counts applies.

## The backbill limit the rule turns on

| Meter type | Backbill limit (months) |
|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 6 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 6 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 6 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 12 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 12 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 12 |

## Truth table

| Zero-kWh bill within the limit window | Set by failed-meter replacement or test exchange | Within-tolerance result on record | Bills covered |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Any | Any | As many of the most recent bills as there are zero-kWh bills |
| No | Yes | No | All whole calendar months from installation to the test date, at most the backbill limit |
| No | Yes | Yes | Neither count applies |
| No | No | Any | Neither count applies |

## Hypothetical cases

- A Standard AMI Smart Meter (limit 6) whose agreement shows four zero-kWh bills among the regular bills ending in the 6 months before the test: the 4 most recent bills are covered.
- An AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter (limit 12) set by a test exchange 9 whole calendar months before the test, never found within tolerance, with no zero-kWh bill: 9 bills are covered. Had it been set 15 months before, 12 would be covered.

title: Demand Charges Recovered When a Metering Service Meter Stops Registering
content:
On an Electric Service Agreement billed on a schedule with a demand charge, whether a **Metering Service** non-registering backbill recovers demand charges depends on whether the demand register failed with the meter, as the measured demand on the covered bills shows.

**Register failed.** Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and covered bills recorded zero measured demand, the demand register failed with the meter, and the demand charges recovered are the prior-year bills' demand charges minus the demand charges already billed on the covered bills.

**Register kept working.** Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and no covered bill recorded zero measured demand, the demand register kept working and no demand charge is recovered.

**No demand charge on the schedule.** Neither treatment applies.

## Input, judgement, output

| Schedule carries a demand charge | Covered bill with zero measured demand | Demand charges recovered |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | At least one | Prior-year bills' demand charges less those already billed on the covered bills |
| Yes | None | None |
| No | (not applicable) | Neither treatment applies |

The prior-year bills are the regular bills of the same billing months one year earlier.

## Hypothetical figures

Six covered bills on a demand schedule; the prior-year bills of the same months carried 2,400.00 of demand charges, and the covered bills already billed 600.00 of demand charges.

- Two covered bills show zero measured demand: 2,400.00 less 600.00, so 1,800.00 of demand charges is recovered.
- No covered bill shows zero measured demand: no demand charge is recovered.

title: Overdue Periodic Test Share in Metering Service Non-Registering Backbills
content:
A **Metering Service** non-registering backbill on a meter type with a periodic test interval is reduced by an overdue-test share when the company's periodic test was overdue.

**Overdue months.** The overdue months are the whole calendar months between the later of the meter's installation date and its latest within-tolerance test date and the non-registering test date, less the meter type's periodic test interval in months.

**Clause.** Where the meter type has a periodic test interval and the overdue months exceed the long-overdue margin of 12 months, the company's periodic test was long overdue and the overdue-test share is the long-overdue share of 0.5. Where the meter type has a periodic test interval and the overdue months are above zero but no more than 12, the overdue-test share is the overdue share of 0.75. In every other case the overdue-test share is 1.

## Intervals

| Meter type | Periodic test interval | In months |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter, Standard AMI Smart Meter, AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 0 years, no interval | Share always 1 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 8 years | 96 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 4 years | 48 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 2 years | 24 |

## Both sides of each threshold (hypothetical AMI Interval Demand Meter, interval 48 months)

| Months since the later of installation and the latest within-tolerance test | Overdue months | Overdue-test share |
|---|---|---|
| 48 | 0 | 1 |
| 49 | 1 | 0.75 |
| 60 | 12 | 0.75 |
| 61 | 13 | 0.5 |

title: Metering Service Reporting Share for Customer-Reported Stopped Meters
content:
When the customer of record asked for the test that found a **Metering Service** meter not registering, the non-registering backbill carries a reporting share that depends on how many zero-kWh bills of the Electric Service Agreement had ended before the request.

**Zero-kWh bills reported late.** These are the zero-kWh bills of the covered period whose billing period ended before the month of the latest test request on the meter.

**Clause.** Where the customer of record requested the test that found the meter not registering and no more than the prompt-report number of 2 zero-kWh bills had ended before that request, the reporting share is the prompt-report share of 0.8. Where the customer of record requested that test and more than 2 zero-kWh bills had ended before it, the reporting share is the late-report share of 0.9. In every other case the reporting share is 1.

The test that found the meter not registering is the one asked for by the latest test request on the meter; it was customer-requested when that request carries the reason "customer request".

## Decision table

| Latest test request on the meter | Zero-kWh bills ended before the request | Reporting share |
|---|---|---|
| Customer request | 0, 1 or 2 | 0.8 |
| Customer request | 3 or more | 0.9 |
| Periodic or utility-initiated | Any | 1 |

## Hypothetical cases (monthly bills ending on the last day of the month)

- Zero-kWh bills ended 31 January and 28 February; the customer's request is dated 10 March: 2 had ended before it, share 0.8.
- Zero-kWh bills ended 31 January, 28 February and 31 March; the customer's request is dated 10 April: 3 had ended before it, share 0.9.
- The same bills, but the test was a periodic test: share 1.

title: Metering Service Decision Memo: Correction Target in Referee Backbill Settlements
content:
**Decision.** A **Metering Service** referee backbill settlement corrects the repriced bills to a target registration that depends on the test requests recorded on the meter installation:

- where the meter carries a utility-initiated test request, the referee backbill settlement corrects the repriced bills only to the lower edge of the tolerance band, 100 minus the meter type's accuracy tolerance, and the referee error factor is the absolute value of one minus that edge divided by the referee test's registration percentage;
- where the meter carries a periodic test request and no utility-initiated test request, the referee backbill settlement corrects the repriced bills to 100 minus one half of the meter type's accuracy tolerance, the referee error factor being the absolute value of one minus that figure divided by the referee test's registration percentage;
- where the meter carries neither, no reduced correction target applies.

**Basis.** A request is carried by the meter when it stands on the installation's test record with that reason, whatever its date. A utility-initiated request decides the target even if a periodic request is also on record.

## Targets in figures

| Meter type | Tolerance | Utility-initiated request on record | Periodic request only |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 1.0 | 99.00 | 99.50 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 0.5 | 99.50 | 99.75 |

## Hypothetical figures

An AMI Interval Demand Meter whose referee test registered 97.00, with a utility-initiated request on record: the error factor is the absolute value of one minus 99 divided by 97, that is 0.0206186. With only a periodic request on record it is the absolute value of one minus 99.5 divided by 97, that is 0.0257732.

title: Repricing Demand Charges in Metering Service Referee Backbill Settlements
content:
On an Electric Service Agreement whose rate schedule carries a demand charge, a **Metering Service** referee backbill settlement reprices demand charges according to the billing demand recorded on the repriced bills.

**Clause.** Where the service agreement's rate schedule carries a demand charge and at least one bill the referee backbill settlement reprices was billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand, the settlement reprices the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of every repriced bill plus the demand charges of the repriced bills billed above that minimum. Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and no repriced bill was billed at the minimum billing demand, the settlement reprices the energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of every repriced bill. Where the rate schedule carries no demand charge, no demand charge is repriced; the settlement reprices the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges.

A bill was billed at the minimum billing demand when the billing demand shown on it, in kW, equals the schedule's minimum billing demand.

## Input, judgement, output

- **Input:** the schedule's demand charge and minimum billing demand; the billing demand and demand charge of each repriced bill.
- **Judgement:** does the schedule carry a demand charge; if so, is any repriced bill at the minimum.
- **Output:** the demand charges that join the repriced energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges.

| Demand charge on the schedule | A repriced bill at the minimum | Demand charges repriced |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Those of bills above the minimum only |
| Yes | No | All of them |
| No | (not applicable) | None |

## Hypothetical example

A schedule with a 100 kW minimum billing demand; four repriced bills with billing demands of 100, 100, 130 and 145 kW and demand charges of 900.00, 900.00, 1,170.00 and 1,305.00. Two bills sit at the minimum, so only 1,170.00 and 1,305.00 are repriced, 2,475.00 of demand charges in all. If the first two bills had shown 101 kW instead, no bill would be at the minimum and all four demand charges would be repriced.

title: Metering Service Training Q&A: How Far Back a Referee Backbill Settlement Reaches
content:
For a **Metering Service** referee backbill settlement, the billing months the settlement reaches back follow what the meter's own records show about when the under-registration began. The records read are the meter's installation record (its installation reason and date), the meter's test results, and the effective date of the current rate schedule on the Electric Service Agreement.

## The rule

Where the meter was set by a failed-meter replacement or a test exchange and has no within-tolerance test result on record, the error is dated from the installation and the billing months the referee backbill settlement reaches back are all the whole calendar months between the installation date and the company test date.

Where the meter has a within-tolerance test result on record and the service agreement's current rate schedule took effect after the latest such result, the billing months the referee backbill settlement reaches back are the whole calendar months between the schedule's effective date and the company test date.

In every other case neither of these datings applies.

## Questions the rule answers

**The meter went in as a failed-meter replacement and has never tested within tolerance. Where does the reach-back start?** At the installation date: every whole calendar month from installation to the company test date is reached back.

**The meter tested within tolerance once and the agreement later moved to a new schedule. Where does it start?** At the date the current schedule took effect, provided that date is after the latest within-tolerance result.

**The meter was set by a test exchange but did test within tolerance later.** The installation dating does not apply, because a within-tolerance result is on record; the schedule dating applies only if the current schedule took effect after that result.

**The schedule took effect on the same day as the latest within-tolerance result.** It did not take effect after it, so the schedule dating does not apply.

## Hypothetical illustration

A meter set on 14 August 2023 by a failed-meter replacement, never tested within tolerance, with a company test on 30 June 2025: the whole calendar months from 14 August 2023 to 30 June 2025 are 22, and all 22 are reached back.

title: Bills After the Company Test in Metering Service Referee Backbill Settlements
content:
A **Metering Service** referee backbill settlement may also reprice regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement whose billing period ended after the company test date, according to the meter installation's status and removal date.

**Removed after the company test.** Where the meter was removed from service after the company test date, the referee backbill settlement also reprices the regular bills whose billing period ended after the company test date and on or before the removal date, added to the bills counted back from the company test date, because the meter kept registering slow until it was taken out.

**Still in service.** Where the meter is still in service, the referee backbill settlement also reprices every regular bill whose billing period ended after the company test date, added to the bills counted back from the company test date.

**Every other case.** In every other case, a meter removed on or before the company test date among them, no bill whose billing period ended after the company test date is added.

## Timeline cases (hypothetical dates, company test on 15 April)

| Installation status and removal date | Bills ending after 15 April that are added |
|---|---|
| Removed on 20 June | Those ending after 15 April and on or before 20 June |
| Removed on 15 April | None, the removal is not after the company test date |
| In service | Every regular bill ending after 15 April |

With monthly bills ending on the last day of each month, a meter removed on 20 June adds the bills ending 30 April and 31 May; the bill ending 30 June ended after the removal date and is not added. A meter still in service on a handling date in late July adds the bills ending 30 April, 31 May and 30 June.

title: Customer Care Note on Metering Service Referee Backbill Settlements
content:
A referee backbill settlement closes a dispute in which the customer of record asked for a Commission referee test of a **Metering Service** meter that the company's own test, the latest result taken by the test method of the meter's type, found slow, and the referee test, which is the meter's latest test result, also found it slow.

**The customer's acceptance.** The settlement is the customer's own acceptance of the referee result: it is recorded as a backbill on the meter's adjustment record against the referee test result on the date the customer accepts it, and a customer who does not accept it has no settlement recorded.

**When the amount is fixed.** The referee backbill settlement is fixed only after the company test result it reviews carries its slow-meter backbill on the meter's adjustment record. Put the other way round, while the meter's adjustment record shows no slow-meter backbill against the company test result under review, no settlement amount is fixed.

| Record | What it shows for a settlement |
|---|---|
| The meter's test results | The company test (latest result by the type's test method) classifies the meter slow, and the meter's latest result, the referee test, also classifies it slow |
| The meter's adjustment record | The slow-meter backbill standing against the company test result; after acceptance, the settlement entry against the referee test result |

## The acceptance tool: `accept_referee_backbill_settlement_27524241`

**Capability.** The customer accepts the outcome of a Commission referee test of the meter that found it slow, settling the dispute over the meter's backbill. One call records the accepted settlement as one backbill entry on the meter's adjustment record, dated today and tied to the referee test result; the entry carries the settlement amount in US dollars that the customer agrees to owe on top of whatever backbill already stands for the meter. Nothing else on the meter or the service account is changed by the call.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool. The representative unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs `accept_referee_backbill_settlement_27524241` with `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

- `meter_installation_id` — the meter installation reference number of the meter the referee tested, as given to the customer by the representative from the meter installation lookup. Identifier text.
- `meter_test_id` — the reference number of the referee test result being accepted, not the request, as given to the customer by the representative from the meter test lookup. Identifier text.
- `settlement_amount` — the settlement the customer accepts, in US dollars, as a non-negative number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed, exactly as the representative stated it.

**Return.** A one-line confirmation: "Referee settlement (settlement reference) accepted on meter (installation reference) for referee result (referee result reference): (amount) USD on (date)." The settlement reference is the new entry's reference number, the amount is shown with 2 decimals and the date is today's acceptance date. Receiving the line means the settlement entry exists on the meter's adjustment record and shows when the meter's adjustments are looked up.

title: Billing Adjustments Memorandum: Amount of a Metering Service Referee Backbill Settlement
content:
The amount of a **Metering Service** referee backbill settlement is defined from two test results of the meter and from the regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement at the premise.

**Definitions.** The company test is the latest test result of the meter taken by the test method of the meter's type; its test date is the company test date. The referee test is the meter's latest test result; its registration percentage is the referee registration.

**Clause.** The referee backbill settlement reprices whole regular bills of the service agreement: counting back from the company test date, the most recent regular bills whose billing period ended on or before that date, as many as the smaller of the billing months the referee backbill settlement reaches back and the referee settlement limit. The billing months the referee backbill settlement reaches back are one half of the whole calendar months between the later of the meter's installation date and the test date of its latest within-tolerance result, and the company test date, rounded down to a whole month, and the referee settlement limit is the meter type's backbill limit. The charges the referee backbill settlement reprices are the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of those bills, corrected to full registration, so that the referee error factor is the absolute value of one minus 100 divided by the referee registration. The referee backbill settlement is the repriced charges times the referee error factor, rounded to the cent, minus every backbill already standing on the meter's adjustment record, never less than 0.00, and a settlement smaller than the meter type's adjustment threshold is recorded as 0.00.

Whole calendar months are counted from a day of one month to the same day of a later month; a month not completed is not counted.

## Where each input is read

| Input | Read from |
|---|---|
| Company test date | The meter's test results, latest result by the type's test method |
| Referee registration | The meter's test results, latest result of any method |
| Installation date and latest within-tolerance test date | The installation record and the meter's test results |
| Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges | The regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement |
| Backbills already standing | The meter's adjustment record, every backbill entry |
| Backbill limit and adjustment threshold | The meter type's billing adjustment limits |

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Latest within-tolerance result 5 May 2023, later than the installation date; company test date 12 March 2025; referee registration 97.50; a meter type with a 12-month backbill limit and a 5.00 threshold.

1. Whole calendar months from 5 May 2023 to 12 March 2025: 22. One half: 11 billing months reached back; the smaller of 11 and 12 is 11 bills.
2. Energy charges of those 11 bills 1,650.00 and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges 330.00: repriced charges 1,980.00.
3. Referee error factor: the absolute value of one minus 100 divided by 97.5, that is 0.0256410.
4. 1,980.00 times 0.0256410 is 50.77 after rounding to the cent.
5. Backbills already standing on the adjustment record: 44.00. 50.77 less 44.00 is 6.77, which is not below 5.00, so the settlement is 6.77.

Had 55.00 already stood on the adjustment record, 50.77 less 55.00 would fall below zero and the settlement would be 0.00.

title: Metering Service Referee Settlement Limits: New Meters and Overdue Periodic Tests
content:
| Meter age and test history at the company test date | Referee settlement limit |
|---|---|
| Installed fewer than 12 whole calendar months before the company test date (the settlement new-meter period) | 6 months (the settlement new-meter limit) |
| Installed 12 whole calendar months or more before the company test date, the meter type has a periodic test interval, and the whole calendar months between the later of the installation date and the latest within-tolerance test date and the company test date exceed that interval | 3 months (the settlement overdue-test limit) |
| Any other meter | No new-meter or overdue-test limit applies |

The limit above bounds the number of whole regular bills a **Metering Service** referee backbill settlement reprices when counting back from the company test date.

**Clause.** Where the meter was installed fewer than the settlement new-meter period of whole calendar months before the company test date, the referee settlement limit is the settlement new-meter limit. Where the meter was installed the settlement new-meter period or more before the company test date, the meter type has a periodic test interval, and the whole calendar months between the later of the installation date and the latest within-tolerance test date and the company test date exceed that interval, the referee settlement limit is the settlement overdue-test limit.

## Intervals by meter type

- Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter, Standard AMI Smart Meter and AMI Bidirectional Net Meter: 0 years, no periodic test interval, so the overdue-test limit never applies.
- AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter: 8 years, 96 whole calendar months.
- AMI Interval Demand Meter: 4 years, 48 whole calendar months.
- Primary Metering Installation: 2 years, 24 whole calendar months.

## Boundary pairs (hypothetical meters)

- Installed 11 whole calendar months before the company test: limit 6. Installed exactly 12: the new-meter limit does not apply.
- AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter, installed long ago, 96 whole calendar months since its latest within-tolerance test: 96 does not exceed 96, no overdue limit. At 97 months: limit 3.
- Primary Metering Installation, installed 40 months before the company test and tested within tolerance 25 months before it: 25 exceeds 24, limit 3.

title: Metering Service Billing Note: Demand Charges in a Referee Refund Settlement
content:
A **Metering Service** referee refund settlement on an Electric Service Agreement billed on a schedule with a demand charge reprices demand charges according to the billing demand of the repriced bills.

| The schedule carries a demand charge | A repriced bill was billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand | Charges repriced |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | At least one | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of every repriced bill, plus the demand charges of the repriced bills billed above the minimum |
| Yes | None | Energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of every repriced bill |
| No | (not applicable) | Energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges; no demand charge |

**Formal statement.** Where the service agreement's rate schedule carries a demand charge and at least one bill the referee refund settlement reprices was billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand, the settlement reprices the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of every repriced bill plus the demand charges of the repriced bills billed above that minimum. Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and no repriced bill was billed at the minimum billing demand, the settlement reprices the energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of every repriced bill.

**Billed at the minimum** means the bill's billing demand in kW equals the schedule's minimum billing demand.

**Hypothetical pair.** Five repriced bills on a schedule with a 75 kW minimum, of which one shows 75 kW: the demand charges of the other four are repriced. If that bill had shown 76 kW, the demand charges of all five would be repriced.

title: Metering Service Training Q&A: Reach-Back of a Referee Refund Settlement
content:
For a **Metering Service** referee refund settlement, the billing months the settlement reaches back follow the meter's own records and the Electric Service Agreement's schedule history.

**The rule.** Where the meter's latest within-tolerance result already lay in the outer drift share of 0.75 of the tolerance band, on the same side of 100 as the company test's registration percentage, the meter was drifting toward the limit at that test, so the error is dated from that test itself rather than from the midpoint, and the billing months the referee refund settlement reaches back are all the whole calendar months between the test date of that within-tolerance result and the company test date. Where the latest within-tolerance result shows no such drift and the service agreement's current rate schedule took effect after its test date, the billing months the referee refund settlement reaches back are the whole calendar months between the schedule's effective date and the company test date. In every other case neither dating applies.

## Questions the rule answers

**What counts as the outer drift share?** A result lying at least 0.75 of the meter type's tolerance away from 100. For a 2.0-point tolerance that is 1.50 points, for a 1.0-point tolerance 0.75 points, and for the 0.5-point tolerance of the Primary Metering Installation 0.375 points.

**Which side of 100 matters?** The side of the company test. The company test found the meter fast, so the latest within-tolerance result must also lie above 100: for a 2.0-point tolerance, at 101.50 or above.

**What if the latest within-tolerance result sat at 98.40 on a 2.0-point type?** It is 1.60 points away, but below 100, the opposite side from a fast company result, so it is not drift.

**What if the schedule changed on the same day as that result?** It did not take effect after the result, so the schedule dating does not apply.

## Hypothetical case

An AMI Interval Demand Meter (tolerance 1.0) tested within tolerance at 100.80 on 1 February 2024 and found fast by the company test on 15 September 2025: 100.80 is 0.80 above 100, at least 0.75, so the reach-back is every whole calendar month from 1 February 2024 to 15 September 2025, that is 19.

title: Metering Service Rule on Late Payment Charges in Referee Refund Settlements
content:
Late payment charges posted on the Electric Service Agreement within the whole calendar months a **Metering Service** referee refund settlement reprices, counted from the handling date as the repriced bills are, were computed on overstated bills, and the settlement reprices them according to the agreement's schedule.

- **General service.** Where the agreement is on a general service schedule (GS, GST, GD or LP) and such late payment charges exist, the repriced late payment charges are those charges times the referee refund error factor, rounded to the cent.
- **Residential.** Where the agreement is on a residential schedule (RS, RT or REV) and such late payment charges exist, the repriced late payment charges are all of those charges.
- **None posted.** Where no late payment charge was posted within those months, no late payment charge is repriced.

The months are the same span of months, reckoned back from the handling date, that selects the repriced bills.

## Examples (hypothetical)
