| Schedule | Late payment charges in the repriced months | Referee refund error factor | Repriced late payment charges |
|---|---|---|---|
| GST | 18.40 | 0.0243902 | 18.40 times 0.0243902, rounded: 0.45 |
| REV | 18.40 | 0.0243902 | 18.40, in full |
| LP | None | Any | None |

title: Referee Refund Settlement Limits by Rate Schedule, Metering Service
content:
**Clause.** For a **Metering Service** referee refund settlement, where the Electric Service Agreement is on Schedule LP, the referee refund limit is the settlement large-power limit of 3 months. Where the agreement is on Schedule GD, the referee refund limit is the settlement medium-demand limit of 6 months. On any other schedule neither limit applies.

| Schedule of the agreement | Referee refund limit |
|---|---|
| Schedule LP Large Power Service | 3 months |
| Schedule GD Medium General Demand Service | 6 months |
| Schedule RS, RT, REV, GS or GST | Neither limit applies |

The schedule is the one recorded on the service agreement.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A settlement on a Schedule GD agreement whose billing months reached back are 9 reprices no more than 6 bills counted back from the company test date; on Schedule LP, no more than 3.

title: Metering Service Referee Refund Settlements and Bills After the Company Test
content:
A **Metering Service** referee refund settlement may reach bills of the Electric Service Agreement that ended after the company test date, according to the meter installation's status and removal date.

**Clause.** Where the meter was removed from service after the company test date, the referee refund settlement also reprices the regular bills whose billing period ended after the company test date and on or before the removal date, added to the bills counted back from the company test date, because the meter kept registering fast until it was taken out. Where the meter is still in service, the referee refund settlement also reprices every regular bill whose billing period ended after the company test date, added to the bills counted back. In every other case, a meter removed on or before the company test date among them, no bill whose billing period ended after the company test date is added.

## Cases (hypothetical, company test on 9 January, monthly bills ending on the 20th)

| Installation record | Bills ending after 9 January that are added |
|---|---|
| Removed 25 February | Those ending 20 January and 20 February |
| Removed 15 February | Only the bill ending 20 January |
| Removed 9 January | None |
| In service, handling date 5 April | Those ending 20 January, 20 February and 20 March |

title: Customer Care Note on Metering Service Referee Refund Settlements
content:
A referee refund settlement closes a dispute in which the customer of record asked for a Commission referee test of a **Metering Service** meter that the company's own test, the latest result taken by the test method of the meter's type, found fast, and the referee test, which is the meter's latest test result, also found it fast.

**The customer's acceptance.** The settlement is the customer's own acceptance of the referee result: it is credited as a refund on the meter's adjustment record against the referee test result on the date the customer accepts it, and a customer who does not accept it has no settlement credited.

**When it is credited.**

- The referee refund settlement is not credited until the company test result it reviews carries its fast-meter refund on the meter's adjustment record.
- The referee refund settlement is not credited until every test result on the customer's other meters that found a meter not registering carries its non-registering backbill on that meter's adjustment record.

Read against the records, the settlement stays uncredited while the meter's adjustment record shows no fast-meter refund against the company test result under review, and while any not-registering result on another meter of the customer has no non-registering backbill on that other meter's adjustment record.

## The acceptance tool: `accept_referee_refund_settlement_2157b6a7`

**Capability.** The customer accepts the outcome of a Commission referee test of the meter that found it fast, settling the dispute over the meter's refund. One call records the accepted settlement as one refund entry on the meter's adjustment record, dated today and tied to the referee test result; the entry carries the settlement amount in US dollars owed back to the customer on top of whatever refund already stands for the meter. Nothing else on the meter or the service account is changed by the call.

**How it is invoked.** It is the customer's own tool: the representative unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs `accept_referee_refund_settlement_2157b6a7` with `call_user_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `meter_installation_id` | The meter installation reference number of the meter the referee tested, as given to the customer by the representative from the meter installation lookup | Identifier text |
| `meter_test_id` | The reference number of the referee test result, not the request, being accepted, as given to the customer by the representative from the meter test lookup | Identifier text |
| `settlement_amount` | The settlement the customer accepts, in US dollars, exactly as the representative stated it | A non-negative number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed |

**Return.** One confirmation line: "Referee refund settlement (settlement reference) accepted on meter (installation reference) for referee result (referee result reference): (amount) USD on (date)." The settlement reference is the new entry's reference number, the amount carries 2 decimals and the date is today's acceptance date. Receiving it means the settlement entry exists on the meter's adjustment record and shows when the meter's adjustments are looked up.

title: Metering Service Referee Refund Settlement: Amount Clause and Worked Example
content:
**Terms.** For a **Metering Service** meter, the company test is the meter's latest test result taken by the test method of the meter's type, and the company test date is its test date. The referee test is the meter's latest test result, and the referee registration is its registration percentage.

**Bills repriced.** The referee refund settlement reprices whole regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement: counting back from the company test date, the most recent regular bills whose billing period ended on or before that date, as many as the smaller of the billing months the referee refund settlement reaches back and the referee refund limit, and no bill whose billing period ended after the company test date. The billing months reached back are one half of the whole calendar months between the later of the meter's installation date and the test date of its latest within-tolerance result, and the company test date, rounded down to a whole month. The referee refund limit is the meter type's refund limit.

**Charges and error factor.** The charges the referee refund settlement reprices are the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of those bills, and the referee refund error factor is the absolute value of one minus 100 divided by the referee registration. No late payment charge is repriced and no interest is added; the repriced late payment charges and the settlement interest are each 0.00.

**Amount.** The referee refund settlement is the repriced charges times the referee refund error factor, rounded to the cent, plus the repriced late payment charges, plus the settlement interest, plus every repeat test fee standing on the meter's metering charges, minus every refund already standing on the meter's adjustment record, never less than 0.00. A settlement smaller than the meter type's adjustment threshold is credited as 0.00.

A whole calendar month runs from a day of one month to the same day of a later month.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Latest within-tolerance result on 8 August 2023, later than installation; company test on 8 August 2025; referee registration 102.50; a type with a 12-month refund limit and a 1.00 threshold.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Whole calendar months, 8 August 2023 to 8 August 2025 | 24 |
| Billing months reached back, one half rounded down | 12 |
| Bills repriced, the smaller of 12 and 12 | 12 |
| Energy plus Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of those bills | 2,400.00 and 600.00, total 3,000.00 |
| Referee refund error factor, absolute value of one minus 100 divided by 102.5 | 0.0243902 |
| Repriced charges times the factor, rounded to the cent | 73.17 |
| Repeat test fees standing on the metering charges | 45.00 |
| Refunds already standing on the adjustment record | 80.00 |
| Settlement: 73.17 plus 45.00 less 80.00 | 38.17, not below 1.00 |

Had 130.00 of refunds already stood on the adjustment record, the result would fall below zero and the settlement would be 0.00.

title: Settlement Interest on Metering Service Referee Refund Settlements
content:
A **Metering Service** referee refund settlement carries settlement interest according to how many bills it counts back from the company test date.

**Clause.** Where the referee refund settlement counts back at least the settlement full-interest number of 12 bills, the settlement interest rate is the settlement interest rate of 4.17 percent (0.0417). Where it counts back at least the settlement half-interest number of 3 bills but fewer than 12, the settlement interest rate is one half of the settlement interest rate, 2.085 percent. In every other case there is no settlement interest.

**Amount.** The settlement interest is the repriced charges times the referee refund error factor, rounded to the cent, times the settlement interest rate, times the number of bills counted back from the company test date divided by 24, which is simple interest for half the repriced period in years, rounded to the cent. Bills whose billing period ended after the company test date are not among the bills counted back.

## Both sides of each threshold

| Bills counted back | Rate |
|---|---|
| 2 | None |
| 3 | 2.085 percent |
| 11 | 2.085 percent |
| 12 | 4.17 percent |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

Repriced charges times the referee refund error factor, rounded, of 73.17, with 12 bills counted back: 73.17 times 0.0417 times 12 divided by 24 is 1.53 after rounding to the cent. With 4 bills counted back: 73.17 times 0.02085 times 4 divided by 24 is 0.25.

title: Counting Earlier Customer Tests on Demand-Billed Agreements, Metering Service
content:
On a **Metering Service** meter whose Electric Service Agreement is billed on a rate schedule that carries a demand charge, the earlier customer-requested tests counted for a repeat test fee follow the meter's own test record, because on demand schedules a periodic company test of the installation is the accuracy check of record.

**Periodic test on record.** Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and the meter carries a periodic test request, that periodic test starts the count afresh, and the earlier customer-requested tests counted are those requested after the meter's latest periodic test request, whenever they fall.

**No periodic test on record.** Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and the meter carries no periodic test request, every earlier customer-requested test of the meter since its installation is counted.

**Schedules without a demand charge.** The count is not reset by a periodic test and is not extended back to installation in these ways.

The charged test itself is not one of the earlier tests it is counted against.

## Truth table

| Schedule carries a demand charge | Periodic test request on the meter | Earlier customer-requested tests counted |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Those requested after the latest periodic test request, whenever they fall |
| Yes | No | Every one since installation |
| No | Yes or no | Not reset or extended in these ways |

## Hypothetical case

A meter on a demand schedule has customer requests on 3 February 2022, 9 May 2023 and 14 June 2023, a periodic test request on 1 March 2023, and a charged customer request on 2 October 2025. The periodic request of 1 March 2023 starts the count afresh: the requests of 9 May 2023 and 14 June 2023 are counted, however long ago they were, and the request of 3 February 2022 is not. Two earlier tests are counted. Without the periodic request on record, all three earlier requests would be counted.

title: Metering Service Repeat Test Escalation Multipliers
content:
| Earlier customer-requested tests of the same meter counted before the charged test's request | Repeat escalation multiplier |
|---|---|
| Three or more | 2.0 (the third-repeat multiplier) |
| Exactly two | 1.5 (the second-repeat multiplier) |
| One or none | 1, no escalation |

**Clause.** Under the **Metering Service**, the repeat escalation multiplier rests on the earlier customer-requested tests of the same meter counted before the charged test's request, the charged test's request being the meter's latest customer-requested test request. Where three or more earlier customer-requested tests are counted, the repeat escalation multiplier is the third-repeat multiplier of 2.0. Where exactly two are counted, the repeat escalation multiplier is the second-repeat multiplier of 1.5. In every other case the repeat escalation multiplier is 1.

## Both sides of each step

| Earlier tests counted | Multiplier |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 1.5 |
| 3 | 2.0 |
| 4 | 2.0 |

The step from 1.5 to 2.0 is reached at three counted tests; a fourth or later counted test does not raise the multiplier further.

**Hypothetical figure.** A base test fee of 150.00 with two earlier tests counted is escalated to 150.00 times 1.5, that is 225.00; with three counted it becomes 300.00.

title: Metering Service Repeat Test Fee Amount: Computation Clause
content:
**Clause.** The **Metering Service** repeat test fee is the base test fee multiplied by the repeat escalation multiplier, plus the witness surcharge, minus the band credit, rounded to the cent once at the end and never less than 0.00. The base test fee is the meter type's repeat test fee; the repeat escalation multiplier is 1, so the fee is not escalated; no witness surcharge is added and no band credit is deducted. The fee is posted on the test date of the result it is charged for.

**Earlier tests counted.** The earlier customer-requested tests counted for the fee are those of the same meter requested within the meter type's free-test period, in whole calendar months, before the charged test's request. Whole calendar months run from a day of one month to the same day of a later month.

## Inputs

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| Meter type's repeat test fee | The meter type's accuracy test terms |
| Meter type's free-test period | The meter type's accuracy test terms |
| Charged result | The meter's latest within-tolerance result answering its latest customer-requested test, with its test date and test method |
| Charged test's request date | The meter's latest customer-requested test request |

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

- A meter type whose repeat test fee is 85.00: the base test fee is 85.00; multiplied by 1 it stays 85.00; with nothing added or deducted and rounding to the cent, the fee is 85.00, posted on the test date of the charged result.
- Counting earlier tests with a 12-month free-test period: the charged test was requested on 20 September 2025. Customer requests on the same meter on 2 November 2024 and 1 October 2024 fall within the 12 whole calendar months before it; a request on 15 August 2024 does not. Two earlier tests are counted.

title: Metering Service Repeat Test Fee: When the Fee Is Owed
content:
**In force.** The **Metering Service** repeat test fee is charged only for a customer-requested test whose result is within tolerance, and only when the count of customer-requested tests in the free-test period for that request already reaches the meter type's free tests per period. That count is taken across every meter installation of the same service agreement, over the meter type's free-test period in calendar months ending the day before the request date of the test, and periodic, utility-initiated and Commission referee tests are not counted in it.

No fee is charged when the meter is found fast, slow or not registering, for periodic or utility-initiated tests, or for the first test in the period. Each test result is charged at most once: a result that already carries a repeat test fee on the meter's charges is not charged again.

**No longer in force.** The clause "the fee is the repeat test fee of the meter type tested and is posted on the test date" is no longer in force; the amount of the fee and its posting date are governed by the current basis for the repeat test fee amount.

## Chargeability at a glance (one free test per period)

| Test reason | Result | Customer-requested tests already counted in the period | Fee owed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer request | Within tolerance | 0 | No, it is the first test in the period |
| Customer request | Within tolerance | 1 or more | Yes |
| Customer request | Fast, slow or not registering | Any | No |
| Periodic | Any | Any | No |
| Utility-initiated | Any | Any | No |

## Hypothetical case

A customer asks for a test in January and again in July of the same year at the same agreement; the meter was exchanged after the January test. The July test finds the meter within tolerance. The January request falls in the free-test period before the July request and is counted even though it was on the earlier meter, so the July result is chargeable once.

title: Metering Service Repeat Test Fee: Desk Guidance and Fee Posting
content:
The **Metering Service** repeat test fee is owed for a chargeable test, which is a customer-requested test whose result is within tolerance when the free-test allowance counted under the agreement-wide allowance rule is already used, and it is charged once for that result. The fee is fixed in amount for the meter's latest within-tolerance result answering the meter's latest customer-requested test, and it is charged for that result.

**Where the fee stands.** A charged repeat test fee stands on the meter's metering charges, tied to the test result it is charged for and dated on that result's test date.

| Record | What it shows |
|---|---|
| The meter's test requests | The latest customer-requested test of the meter |
| The meter's test results | The latest within-tolerance result answering that request |
| The meter's metering charges | Whether that result already carries its repeat test fee |

## Charging the fee: `charge_repeat_test_fee_cae4c873`

**Capability.** The tool charges the repeat test fee owed for a customer-requested accuracy test of a meter that found the meter within tolerance after the customer's free test allowance was used. One call adds one repeat test fee to the meter's metering charges, tied to the test result it is charged for and dated on that result's test date; the fee is the amount in US dollars the customer owes for that test. Nothing else on the meter or the service account is changed by the call.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the representative unlocks `charge_repeat_test_fee_cae4c873` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `meter_installation_id` | The meter installation reference number of the tested meter, as returned by the meter installation lookup | Identifier text |
| `meter_test_id` | The reference number of the test result, not the test request, the fee is charged for, as returned by the meter test lookup for that meter | Identifier text |
| `fee_amount` | The repeat test fee in US dollars | A non-negative number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed |

**Return.** A one-line confirmation: "Repeat test fee (charge reference) charged on meter (installation reference) for test result (test result reference): (amount) USD dated (date)." The charge reference is the new charge's reference number, the amount is shown with 2 decimals, and the date is the test date of the charged result, not the day of the call. Receiving the line means the fee exists on the meter's metering charges and shows when the meter's charges are looked up.

title: Equipment Check Charges in the Metering Service Repeat Test Fee
content:
The base test fee of a **Metering Service** repeat test fee follows how the premises is served, as the Electric Service Agreement shows: its service voltage, and whether its rate schedule carries a demand charge.

**Primary voltage.** Where the service agreement takes service at primary voltage, the instrument transformers are checked with the meter and the base test fee is the meter type's repeat test fee plus the instrument-transformer check charge of 125.00.

**Secondary voltage on a demand schedule.** Where the agreement takes service at secondary voltage on a rate schedule that carries a demand charge, the demand register is checked with the meter and the base test fee is the meter type's repeat test fee plus the demand-register check charge of 40.00.

**Every other case.** No check charge is added to the meter type's repeat test fee.

## Condition table

| Service voltage on the agreement | Schedule carries a demand charge | Check made with the meter | Check charge added to the base test fee (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary | Yes or no | Instrument transformers | 125.00 |
| Secondary | Yes | Demand register | 40.00 |
| Secondary | No | None | None |

## Hypothetical figures

- A Primary Metering Installation, repeat test fee 375.00, on an agreement served at primary voltage: base test fee 375.00 plus 125.00, that is 500.00.
- An AMI Interval Demand Meter, repeat test fee 150.00, on an agreement served at secondary voltage on a schedule with a demand charge: base test fee 150.00 plus 40.00, that is 190.00.
- A Standard AMI Smart Meter, repeat test fee 45.00, on a secondary-voltage residential schedule without a demand charge: no check charge is added.

title: Computation of the Slow-Meter Backbill Amount, Metering Service
content:
The slow-meter backbill of a **Metering Service** meter is the amount computed as follows from the company test result and the regular bills of the Electric Service Agreement at the premise.

## The computation

1. **Company test.** The company test is the latest test result of the meter taken by the test method of the meter's type. Its test date is the company test date and its registration percentage is the company test's registration.
2. **Backbill period.** The slow-meter backbill period is made of whole regular bills of the service agreement: counting back from the company test date, it takes the most recent regular bills whose billing period ended on or before that date, as many as the smaller of the billing months the slow-meter backbill reaches back and the slow-meter backbill limit.
3. **Billing months reached back.** These are one half of the whole calendar months between the later of the meter's installation date and the test date of its latest within-tolerance result, and the company test date, rounded down to a whole month.
4. **Slow-meter backbill limit.** This is the meter type's backbill limit, the longest backbill period of the type.
5. **Corrected charges.** These are the energy charges and the Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of the bills of the period, totalled.
6. **Error factor.** The bills are corrected to full registration, so the slow-meter error factor is the absolute value of one minus 100 divided by the company test's registration.
7. **Backbill.** The slow-meter backbill is the corrected charges times the slow-meter error factor, rounded to the cent once at the end. A slow-meter backbill smaller than the meter type's adjustment threshold is recorded as 0.00.

**Whole calendar months.** A whole calendar month runs from a day of one month to the same day of the next month. The whole calendar months between two dates are the months completed from the earlier date to the later date: from 10 January to 9 July is 5, and from 10 January to 10 July is 6.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

| Input | Hypothetical value |
|---|---|
| Installation date | 10 January 2023 |
| Latest within-tolerance result | None on record |
| Company test date and registration | 25 January 2025, 96.00 |
| Meter type's backbill limit | 6 months |
| Meter type's adjustment threshold | 1.00 |
| Energy charges of the six most recent regular bills ending on or before 25 January 2025 | 540.00 |
| Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of those bills | 90.00 |

- Whole calendar months from 10 January 2023 to 25 January 2025: 24. One half, rounded down: 12 billing months reached back.
- The smaller of 12 and the 6-month limit is 6, so the period is the six most recent regular bills.
- Corrected charges: 540.00 plus 90.00, that is 630.00.
- Error factor: one minus 100 divided by 96 is negative 0.0416667; its absolute value is 0.0416667.
- Backbill: 630.00 times 0.0416667 is 26.25, which is not below 1.00, so the backbill is 26.25.

## Rounding points

- One half of an odd number of months is rounded down: 25 whole calendar months give 12 billing months reached back.
- The amount is rounded once, after the corrected charges are multiplied by the error factor; the bills are not rounded one by one.

title: Slow-Meter Backbills Under the Metering Service: Desk Guidance and Posting
content:
A slow-meter backbill recovers the charges a **Metering Service** meter under-registered, and it is calculated for the company's own test result of the meter, which is the latest test result taken by the test method of the meter's type, when that result classifies the meter slow. The slow-meter backbill is recorded on the meter's adjustment record against that test result, as a backbill, on the date it is calculated.

## When the backbill is due

| Record | What it shows |
|---|---|
| The meter's test results | The latest result taken by the meter type's test method (meter shop or field) classifies the meter slow |
| The meter's adjustment record | Where the slow-meter backbill stands once recorded: a backbill entry tied to that test result, dated the day it was calculated |

The company test result is identified from the meter's own test record: a result taken by a method other than the meter type's test method is not the company's own test for this purpose.

## Recording the backbill: `post_slow_meter_backbill_dc57beb1`

**Capability.** The tool records the slow-meter backbill that Lakeshore calculates for the company's own accuracy test of a meter that registered too little energy. One call adds one backbill entry to the meter's adjustment record, dated today and tied to the test result it corrects; the entry carries the backbill amount in US dollars, and that amount becomes the underbilled charges the customer owes for the meter's error. Nothing else on the meter or the service account is changed by the call.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the representative first unlocks `post_slow_meter_backbill_dc57beb1` with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `meter_installation_id` | The meter installation reference number of the meter whose registration was found slow, as returned by the meter installation lookup | Identifier text |
| `meter_test_id` | The reference number of the test result, not the test request, that the backbill corrects, as returned by the meter test lookup for that meter | Identifier text |
| `backbill_amount` | The backbill in US dollars | A positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed; 0.00 records a backbill below the posting threshold |

**Return.** A one-line confirmation: "Slow-meter backbill (adjustment reference) recorded on meter (installation reference) for test result (test result reference): (amount) USD on (date)." The adjustment reference is the new entry's reference number, the amount is shown with 2 decimals and the date is today's adjustment date. Receiving this line means the backbill entry exists on the meter's adjustment record, and it shows when the meter's adjustments are looked up.

**Illustration (hypothetical references).** For installation MI-0001 and test result MT-0002, a call with a backbill amount of 26.25 returns a line stating that a slow-meter backbill of 26.25 USD was recorded on meter MI-0001 for test result MT-0002 on the current date.

title: Slow-Meter Backbill Limits for New Meters and Overdue Periodic Tests, Metering Service
content:
Two limits bound a **Metering Service** slow-meter backbill according to the meter's age and its test history.

**New meters.** Where the meter was installed fewer than the new-meter period of 12 whole calendar months before the company test date, the slow-meter backbill limit is the new-meter backbill limit of 6 months.

**Overdue periodic test.** Where the meter was installed the new-meter period of 12 whole calendar months or more before the company test date, the meter type has a periodic test interval, and the whole calendar months between the later of the installation date and the latest within-tolerance test date and the company test date exceed that interval, the company's periodic test was overdue and the slow-meter backbill limit is the overdue-test backbill limit of 3 months.

**Every other case.** No new-meter or overdue-test limit applies.

## Periodic test intervals the overdue limit turns on

| Meter type | Periodic test interval | In whole calendar months |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 0 years (no interval) | The overdue limit never applies |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 0 years (no interval) | The overdue limit never applies |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 0 years (no interval) | The overdue limit never applies |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 8 years | 96 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 4 years | 48 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 2 years | 24 |

## Both sides of each threshold (hypothetical meters)

| Case | Months installed before the company test | Months since the later of installation and the latest within-tolerance test | Meter type | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 11 | 11 | Standard AMI Smart Meter | 6 (new meter) |
| B | 12 | 12 | Standard AMI Smart Meter | No new-meter limit; no interval, so no overdue limit |
| C | 60 | 48 | AMI Interval Demand Meter | No overdue limit, since 48 does not exceed 48 |
| D | 60 | 49 | AMI Interval Demand Meter | 3 (overdue) |
| E | 30 | 25 | Primary Metering Installation | 3 (overdue), since 25 exceeds 24 |

The new-meter period is counted from the installation date alone; the overdue count runs from the later of the installation date and the latest within-tolerance test date.

title: Metering Service Rule on the Registration Target for Slow-Meter Backbills After Company-Initiated Tests
content:
The registration to which a **Metering Service** slow-meter backbill corrects the bills depends on the test requests recorded on the meter.

**Utility-initiated test on record.** Where the meter carries a utility-initiated test request, a test the company ordered outside its periodic schedule, the slow-meter backbill corrects the bills only to the lower edge of the tolerance band, 100 minus the meter type's accuracy tolerance, and the slow-meter error factor is the absolute value of one minus that edge divided by the company test's registration percentage.

**Periodic test on record, no utility-initiated test.** Where the meter carries a periodic test request and no utility-initiated test request, the slow-meter backbill corrects the bills to 100 minus one half of the meter type's accuracy tolerance, and the slow-meter error factor is the absolute value of one minus that figure divided by the company test's registration percentage.

**Neither on record.** No reduced correction target applies.

A test request is "carried" by the meter when it is recorded on the meter installation with that test reason, whenever it was made.

## Correction targets by meter type

| Meter type | Accuracy tolerance (points) | Target with a utility-initiated request | Target with a periodic request and no utility-initiated request |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 2.0 | 98.00 | 99.00 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 1.0 | 99.00 | 99.50 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 0.5 | 99.50 | 99.75 |

## Truth table

| Utility-initiated request on the meter | Periodic request on the meter | Correction target |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes or no | 100 minus the tolerance |
| No | Yes | 100 minus one half of the tolerance |
| No | No | No reduced target |

## Hypothetical figures

An AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter found slow at 95.00:

- with a utility-initiated request on record, the error factor is the absolute value of one minus 98 divided by 95, that is 0.0315789;
- with only a periodic request on record, it is the absolute value of one minus 99 divided by 95, that is 0.0421053.

title: Demand Charges in Metering Service Slow-Meter Backbills on Demand-Billed Electric Service Agreements
content:
Where the Electric Service Agreement behind a **Metering Service** meter is billed on a rate schedule that carries a demand charge, the charges a slow-meter backbill corrects depend on whether the bills of the backbill period were billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand. A bill was billed at the minimum billing demand when its billing demand in kW equals the schedule's minimum billing demand.

## The rule

- **Some bills held at the minimum.** Where the service agreement's rate schedule carries a demand charge and at least one bill of the slow-meter backbill period was billed at the schedule's minimum billing demand, the charges the slow-meter backbill corrects are the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of every bill of the period plus the demand charges of the bills billed above that minimum, because a billing demand held at the schedule minimum was not set by the meter.
- **No bill held at the minimum.** Where the rate schedule carries a demand charge and no bill of the slow-meter backbill period was billed at the minimum billing demand, the charges the slow-meter backbill corrects are the energy, Power Supply Cost Recovery and demand charges of every bill of the period.
- **No demand charge.** Where the rate schedule carries no demand charge, no demand charge is corrected; the corrected charges are the energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges.

## Decision table

| Schedule carries a demand charge | Bills of the period billed at the minimum billing demand | Demand charges corrected |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | At least one | Only those of the bills billed above the minimum |
| Yes | None | Those of every bill of the period |
| No | (not applicable) | None |

## Worked example (hypothetical bills)

A schedule with a demand charge and a 50 kW minimum billing demand; the backbill period has six bills.

| Bill | Billing demand | Demand charge | Corrected? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 50 kW | 400.00 | No, held at the minimum |
| 2 | 50 kW | 400.00 | No, held at the minimum |
| 3 | 62 kW | 520.00 | Yes |
| 4 | 73 kW | 610.00 | Yes |
| 5 | 58 kW | 480.00 | Yes |
| 6 | 84 kW | 700.00 | Yes |

Demand charges corrected: 520.00 plus 610.00 plus 480.00 plus 700.00, that is 2,310.00. With energy and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of 3,000.00 across the six bills, the corrected charges are 5,310.00. Had no bill been at 50 kW, all six demand charges would be corrected.

title: Metering Service Billing Desk Note: Dating a Slow Meter's Error From Its Own Records
content:
The billing months a **Metering Service** slow-meter backbill reaches back follow what the meter's own records show about when the under-registration began. The installation record shows why the meter was set, the meter's test results show whether it has a within-tolerance result (a result classifying it within tolerance), and the Electric Service Agreement shows the date its current rate schedule took effect.

## The rule

- **Set by replacement or exchange, never found accurate.** Where the meter was set by a failed-meter replacement or a test exchange and the meter has no within-tolerance test result on record, the error is dated from the installation and the billing months the slow-meter backbill reaches back are all the whole calendar months between the installation date and the company test date.
- **Reprogrammed for a later schedule.** Where the meter has a within-tolerance test result on record and the service agreement's current rate schedule took effect after the test date of the latest such result, the meter was reprogrammed for that schedule and the billing months the slow-meter backbill reaches back are the whole calendar months between the schedule's effective date and the company test date.
- **Every other case.** Neither dating applies; the reach-back is not taken from the installation date or from the schedule's effective date in the ways above.

## Condition table

| Installation reason is failed-meter replacement or test exchange | Within-tolerance result on record | Current schedule took effect after the latest within-tolerance result | Billing months reached back |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | (not applicable) | All whole calendar months from installation to the company test date |
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Whole calendar months from the schedule's effective date to the company test date |
| No | Yes | Yes | Whole calendar months from the schedule's effective date to the company test date |
| Yes | Yes | No | Neither dating applies |
| No | Yes | No | Neither dating applies |
| No | No | (not applicable) | Neither dating applies |

"After" is strict: a schedule that took effect on the very test date of the latest within-tolerance result did not take effect after it.

## Hypothetical cases

- A meter set by a test exchange on 3 April 2023 with no within-tolerance result is found slow on 20 February 2025. The whole calendar months from 3 April 2023 to 20 February 2025 are 22, and all 22 are reached back.
- A meter found within tolerance on 1 June 2023, on an agreement whose current schedule took effect on 15 March 2024, is found slow on 15 November 2024. The whole calendar months from 15 March 2024 to 15 November 2024 are 8, and all 8 are reached back.

title: Metering Service Smart Meter Opt-Out Terms
content:
**Who may opt out.** A customer holding a **Metering Service** meter type that may be opted out of may opt out to a Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter, provided the service agreement is on Schedule RS or GS and has no Net Energy Metering agreement in approved or operating status.

**Whose decision.** Opting out is the customer's own election. It rests on the customer's own statement for the service agreement concerned; the company's records do not make the election.

**Re-election.** The customer may not opt out again within the meter type's re-election lockout, in months, after returning to a communicating meter.

**Fees.** The opt-out setup fee is charged once, on the date the opt-out meter is installed, and the monthly fee for every billing period the opt-out meter is in service. The income-qualified fees replace the standard fees when the customer's income qualification is current, that is when its "income qualified until" date is on or after the fee date. Opt-out fees are charged only while the opt-out meter installation is in service, as the installation record shows.

**Consequences.** Opting out ends eligibility for time-of-use schedules, net energy metering and remote reconnection. Returning to a communicating meter is free.

## Eligibility check

| Condition | Must hold |
|---|---|
| Meter type held may be opted out of | Yes |
| Service agreement schedule | Schedule RS or Schedule GS |
| Net Energy Metering agreement in approved or operating status | None |
| Customer's own election | Stated by the customer |
| Lockout after a return to a communicating meter | Elapsed |

## Fee examples (hypothetical dates)

- Income qualification valid until 31 May; opt-out meter installed on 31 May: the income-qualified setup fee applies, since the qualification date is on the fee date.
- Same qualification; monthly fee for the billing period ending 30 June: the standard monthly fee applies, since the qualification date is before the fee date.
- The opt-out installation was removed on 15 June: no monthly fee is charged for any billing period after it ceased to be in service.

title: Revenue Protection Bulletin: Metering Service Tampering and Diversion Findings
content:
Tampering and diversion at a **Metering Service** premise are established only by a field investigation record, never by a report or a denial over the phone.

**Confirmed findings.** When the field investigation's finding is tampering confirmed or diversion confirmed, the meter type's investigation charge is charged once for that field order, and the estimated unbilled kWh recorded by the investigation is backbilled for up to the meter type's unauthorized-use backbill period at the rates of the affected bills; the normal backbill limit does not apply. A confirmed finding on a residential agreement allows a Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit to be assessed under the Security Deposit program.

**Findings without a charge.** A finding of no tampering, or a visit recorded as no access, carries no charge.

**Once per field order; disputes.** Each field order is charged at most once: a field order that already carries an investigation charge is not charged again. Disputes of a confirmed finding are handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.

## Finding and consequence

| Field investigation finding | Investigation charge | Unbilled kWh backbilled | Residential Unauthorized Use Deposit may be assessed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tampering confirmed | Yes, once for the field order | Yes, up to the unauthorized-use period | Yes, on a residential agreement |
| Diversion confirmed | Yes, once for the field order | Yes, up to the unauthorized-use period | Yes, on a residential agreement |
| No tampering | No | No | No |
| No access | No | No | No |

## Points of judgement

- A caller reporting a neighbour's tampering, or denying tampering, changes nothing; only the field investigation record establishes a finding.
- **Hypothetical case.** A confirmed tampering finding at a Standard AMI Smart Meter premise with 1,800 unbilled kWh recorded: the type's investigation charge is posted once for that field order, and the 1,800 kWh are backbilled at the rates of the affected bills within the type's unauthorized-use period rather than the ordinary backbill limit.

| Meter type | Investigation charge when tampering or diversion is confirmed (USD) | Longest period for which energy used through tampering or diversion is backbilled (months) |
|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 150.00 | 24 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 150.00 | 24 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 150.00 | 24 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 350.00 | 36 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 350.00 | 36 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 750.00 | 36 |

## Points of reference

- The three residential-class types carry a 150.00 charge and a 24-month backbill reach; the AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter and the AMI Interval Demand Meter carry 350.00 and 36 months; the Primary Metering Installation carries 750.00 and 36 months.
- **Hypothetical finding.** A confirmed diversion at a premise with an AMI Interval Demand Meter carries the 350.00 investigation charge, and the unregistered energy is backbilled for no more than 36 months.

title: Classification of Metering Service Test Results Against Tolerance
content:
A test result of the **Metering Service** classifies the meter by its registration percentage, the energy the meter registered as a percentage of true energy to two decimals, against the meter type's accuracy tolerance in percentage points:

- **within tolerance** when the registration percentage is at least 100 minus the tolerance and at most 100 plus the tolerance;
- **fast** when it is above that band;
- **slow** when it is below that band and above zero;
- **not registering** when the meter registered no energy at test load.

Each test request receives one result; a request that already carries a recorded result receives no second one. A meter found fast, slow or not registering is replaced within the meter type's exchange period, in business days, and its billing is corrected under the company's billing adjustment rule for meters found inaccurate. A within-tolerance result closes the request without any billing correction.

## Decision table

| Registration percentage | Classification | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| From 100 minus tolerance up to 100 plus tolerance, both edges included | Within tolerance | Request closed, no billing correction |
| Above 100 plus tolerance | Fast | Meter replaced; billing corrected by a refund |
| Below 100 minus tolerance and above zero | Slow | Meter replaced; billing corrected by a backbill |
| No energy registered at test load | Not registering | Meter replaced; billing corrected by a backbill |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical results)

For a meter type whose tolerance is 2.0 points:

| Registration | Classification |
|---|---|
| 102.00 | Within tolerance (upper edge) |
| 102.01 | Fast |
| 98.00 | Within tolerance (lower edge) |
| 97.99 | Slow |
| No registration at test load | Not registering |

For a meter type whose tolerance is 0.5 points, 100.50 is within tolerance and 100.51 is fast; 99.50 is within tolerance and 99.49 is slow.

title: Witnessed Accuracy Tests: Metering Service Witness Surcharges
content:
A **Metering Service** customer who asks to witness a customer-requested accuracy test and is later charged a repeat test fee for it pays a witness surcharge that depends on where the test was performed.

**Clause.** Where the customer asked to witness the charged test and the test was performed in the field, the witness surcharge is the field witness surcharge of 60.00. Where the customer asked to witness it and it was performed in the meter shop, the witness surcharge is the shop witness surcharge of 25.00. In every other case there is no witness surcharge.

**Records read.** Whether the customer asked to witness the test is shown on the customer-requested test request; where the test was performed is the test method recorded on the charged result.

## Decision table

| Customer asked to witness | Charged result's test method | Witness surcharge (USD) |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Field | 60.00 |
| Yes | Meter shop | 25.00 |
| No | Field or meter shop | None |

## Hypothetical cases

- An AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter tested in place, witnessed at the customer's request: surcharge 60.00.
- A Standard AMI Smart Meter exchanged and tested in the meter shop, witnessed at the customer's request: surcharge 25.00.
- The same shop test with no witness request: no surcharge.

title: Tolerance Band Credit on Metering Service Repeat Test Fees
content:
A **Metering Service** test result that is within tolerance but close to the edge of the tolerance band earns a band credit against the repeat test fee charged for it.

**Band position.** The band position of the charged result is the absolute difference between its registration percentage and 100, divided by the meter type's accuracy tolerance.

**Clause.** Where the band position is at least the outer-quarter share of 0.75, the result sat in the outer quarter of the tolerance band and the band credit is the outer-quarter credit of 100.00. Where the band position is at least the outer-half share of 0.5 and below 0.75, the band credit is the outer-half credit of 50.00. In every other case there is no band credit.

## Band credit by meter type, in registration points away from 100

| Meter type | Tolerance | Outer-quarter credit of 100.00 when the result is off 100 by at least | Outer-half credit of 50.00 when off 100 by at least, and by less than the outer-quarter figure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Communicating Opt-Out Meter | 2.0 | 1.50 | 1.00 |
| Standard AMI Smart Meter | 2.0 | 1.50 | 1.00 |
| AMI Bidirectional Net Meter | 2.0 | 1.50 | 1.00 |
| AMI Three-Phase Commercial Meter | 2.0 | 1.50 | 1.00 |
| AMI Interval Demand Meter | 1.0 | 0.75 | 0.50 |
| Primary Metering Installation | 0.5 | 0.375 | 0.25 |

Results on either side of 100 are treated alike: 98.50 and 101.50 both sit 1.50 points away.

## Both sides of each threshold (hypothetical results, tolerance 2.0)

| Charged result | Points from 100 | Band position | Band credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 101.50 | 1.50 | 0.75 | 100.00 |
| 101.49 | 1.49 | 0.745 | 50.00 |
| 99.00 | 1.00 | 0.5 | 50.00 |
| 99.01 | 0.99 | 0.495 | None |
